evaluations.label: A
errors: Names are misspelled and inconsistent: 'Mark Knopp', 'Xavier Juukens', 'Dirk Mankveld'.
Action item 'Prepare intuitive design concepts' assigned to the User Interface Designer was never assigned in the meeting.
Action item 'Address material considerations for lightweight design' assigned to Xavier was never assigned; he only said the material should be light.
'Dolphin: freedom, smooth design' - nothing in the transcript says the dolphin stands for smooth design.
'Provide personal assignments' is attributed to Mark; the transcript says the personal coach gives them.
'Marketing expert to provide trend input later' and 'Bring marketing insights on user preferences' overstate what Dirk said (he only said he has some ideas).
Timestamps are often off (for example product scope at 10:34, pricing at 12:10).
strengths: Notes the whiteboard responsiveness problem and the preference for pen and paper.
Covers the four animals, scope, accessibility, light material, the price numbers and the 30-minute return.
Has timestamps and an action-item section.
weaknesses: Action items are mostly invented or mis-assigned, which makes the decisions and actions section misleading.
Name errors and a vague UI designer label.
Terse bullets give little context, for example no reason for the 'limited margin' remark.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Names are misspelled: 'Mark Knopf', 'Dirk Mengveld', 'Xavier Jökens'.
'UI designer also present (name not captured)' - he introduced himself as Nick Broer.
'Rational changes only' garbles the UI designer's remark about avoiding revolutionary changes.
'Positioning: fashion electronics' is a reasonable paraphrase, but 'Dirk ... focused on user needs and new product direction' is a loose summary.
strengths: Clear structure: goals, introductions, process, early design considerations, whiteboard exercise.
Gets the €25 selling price and about €12.50 production cost right, and flags the tight budget.
Correctly captures that personal assignments come via the personal coach, that the next meeting is in 30 minutes, and that minutes go in the shared folder.
weaknesses: No explicit action-item or owner section; Dirk's pending marketing ideas are not captured.
Does not mention the whiteboard responsiveness issue.

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'TS3012a' project code does not appear in the transcript.
Names are wrong or inconsistent: 'Markoff', 'Dirk Mangfelt', 'Savier Jokins'; the UI designer is only 'Speaker 4'.
'Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope ... is limited to a TV remote' - the UI designer asked the question and the Project Manager clarified.
'Lightweight materials that are aesthetically impactful' - aesthetic impact was not said.
'Savier ... tasked with determining internal components, materials and aesthetics' is a paraphrase of his three questions, but the roles list is repeated several times, padding the notes.
Action items (research market trends; design a distinctive interface) were not assigned in the meeting and have no owners.
Open questions are framed as unresolved, but the light-material and accessibility points were stated as considerations, not open questions.
strengths: Most detailed outline of the meeting, including all four animals and what each stood for.
Has the €25 and €12.50 figures and the 30-minute reconvene.
Includes a separate section of open design questions.
weaknesses: Invented project code and generic, unowned action items.
Redundant structure (summary, roles, outline repeat the same facts).
Speaker labels and mangled names reduce usefulness for someone who missed the meeting.
Does not mention that Dirk has marketing ideas still to share or that the coach hands out assignments by name.

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Dirk Mengveld' is misspelled in the action item.
Timestamps are approximate and a few are off by a minute or more.
'The interface designer urged familiarity and rational changes' repeats the garbled transcript wording.
strengths: Attributes statements to the right people: dolphin to the UI designer, elephant to Dirk, tiger to Xavier, ant to Mark, scope question to the UI designer and answer to Mark.
Captures the whiteboard responsiveness problem, the €25 / €12.50 numbers and the comment that there is not much room to work with.
Correctly records that Dirk has ideas but has not prepared them, that the personal coach gives individual assignments, and the 30-minute reconvene.
Single action item is grounded in the transcript and has an owner.
weaknesses: Only one action item; does not list Mark putting minutes in the folder or the personal coach assignments as actions.
The summary is somewhat generic and the animal-exercise detail is wordy.
Does not name the UI designer.

rationale: D is the most faithful: speakers and statements are attributed correctly, numbers are right, it captures the whiteboard issue and Dirk's pending ideas, and its one action item is real. B is accurate and well organised with the key numbers and next steps but has no action-item section and misses the UI designer's name. C is the most detailed outline but invents a project code, uses speaker labels and mangled names, misattributes the scope clarification, and lists generic unowned action items. A has the weakest decisions and actions: its owner-assigned items (UI designer preparing concepts, Xavier addressing materials) were never assigned, and names are wrong.
